x: I understand that George Powell, the Club's strong man in field events, and who incidently was a prominent factor in Surrey gaining third place in last year's Inter-County contest, is contemplating entering for the Decathlon at the forthcoming A.A.A.
He has jumped more than 21-ft., and, like our members Powell and Pollard, he is very enthusiastic. It is up to these men to see that their activities are developed in the club.

Looking through the list of sufferers, one sees such names as McMullen and Odell (Irish); Williams, Davis, Davies, Thomas and Powell (Welsh); Fletcher, Mitchell, Crighton, Stewart and McKay (Scotch); and Merlin (Cornish).

The excitement was now mounting in the crowd and encouraging cheers were given to the Bels in the last event on the cinders, the 1 mile Medley Relay. Brown, Basan, Vargas and Powell turned out for the L.A.C. and Jarvis, Cook, Port and T.

Points were scored for this Shield in the High Jump, Long Jump, Javelin and Shot Putt events, and George Powell, our Field Events Captain, succeeded in winning the Shield for the first time, closely followed, however, by B.
Chantler, Cook, McKay, McLean, Poulter, Powell, Redgrave, Rollins and J.
Meantime, Powell had been trying to leave Tosh, but those long strides of Tosh took him home a winner by 2 yds., with Kench a few yards away. 4 points to Belgrave.
Turner won the Javelin event with a throw of 167ft. 9½in. and Powell was third, throwing 161ft. 7½in.; Tom Scrimshaw was successful in the scratch 880yds. race in 2min. 0 4-5sec.

Jones, earlier in the afternoon, had finished second in the half-mile handicap. Powell, who always seems to be placed in this event, finished third. The final of this event was the last race of the afternoon.
Powell, L.A.C., and Tommy Scrimshaw, in opposition, and Powell proved the victor after a fast run race.
Powell, fifth, gained a standard medal. Harold King was another to gain a standard medal, his effort being in the Seven Miles Walk.
Powell. These three swept down the finishing straight together, with Gutteridge snatching a win from Powell in the last yard, with our Tommy a yard or so out.
Powell (3rd A.A.A.
The finalists were Hampson, Peltzer, Townend, Powell, Carr and Johannessen, and, I think, the most classical field I have been in. I drew sixth position, with Hampson fifth and Powell seventh.
He was followed by Edwards (Navy), Powell, the Oxford Blue, in the colours of Thames H. and H., Tommy Marchant (Horsham B.S.) and Townsend (Westbury).
Our representatives, Powell and Melchior, were definitely superior to the L.A.C. men in the Javelin, and George showed good form for one who is as yet not warmed up.

In the Javelin, Powell (164ft. 1in.) and Melchior (148ft 0in.) took first and third positions. Pfenninger won the Weight Putt for us with a magnificent effort of 39ft. 6in., and also took second place in the Discus Throw (116ft. 5½in.) and fourth in the High Jump (5ft. 6in.).

Melchior and Powell were unable to throw, owing to the claims of work, but Quack's win is the reward of persistence. When he matures physically, he will throw 160ft.
The Medley relay was a very close race, Belgrave winning from the Police in 3 mins. 46 secs. Syd Jones, Jeal, Powell and T.
Jones showed he had lost none of his form with a first and second, and Charlie Melchior proved that his working arm was in good throwing order and was well backed up by the evergreen George Powell.

Marchant strode out in fine style, however, and soon caught his man and carried on to give us yet another win. In the Field Events, Charlie Melchior gained us first place in the Javelin with George Powell second, and A.

Miska won the Discus handicap from George Powell and the Hop, Step and Jump handicap was won by Ian Forrester. Also on the programme was an 880 yards novices race, open to unattached competitors, but we only had three starters for this and one wonders if there are any unattached athletes about, espe…

Edwards as previously stated won the javelin with Liggins 2nd and Powell 3rd. On the whole it was a most satisfactory Championship day but it would greatly help in the smooth running of the programme if members would enter BEFORE the day so that we get a programme with the correct names on.

Chris Powley battled with English Schools runner-up Powell in the 200m and just finished 2nd. Stuart King, as dependable as ever, got two seconds in the shot and discus, and Phil Clay also took second in the 'B' shot.
